title: Engineering Leader
description:
About Ema

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Leader to manage and scale multiple product lines in the Voice, BPO, and Workforce Management space. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of real-time voice systems, operations research, and data-intensive platform engineering.

You will report directly to the Head of Engineering and own the engineering organization that builds the infrastructure powering Ema’s Voice AI Employees, Agent QA, auto-learning pipelines, rich analytics, and workforce optimization capabilities — all operating as scalable, multi-tenant systems deployed across global geographies.

You will collaborate with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to translate customer needs into production systems that handle high volumes of voice data, deliver real-time insights, and continuously improve through automated learning loops. As the owner of multiple product lines, you will balance roadmap priorities across Voice, BPO operations, and WFM (work force management) — ensuring each product evolves cohesively while meeting distinct customer needs.

What You Will Do

Scalable Multi-Tenant Systems

  • Architect and build multi-tenant systems that serve enterprise customers across geographies with strict data residency, isolation, and compliance requirements.

  • Design high-throughput ingestion systems capable of processing large volumes of voice data, call metadata, and operational telemetry in near real-time.

  • Make foundational architectural decisions on data stores, stream processing, and storage tiers — balancing query performance, cost, and operational simplicity.

  • Champion SOLID principles, clean architecture, and engineering rigor across all codebases — ensuring systems are testable, extensible, and maintainable at scale.

Team Building & Engineering Culture

  • Recruit, hire, and develop senior engineers across a multi-disciplinary function spanning voice engineering, backend systems, data engineering, and applied operations research.

  • Establish engineering standards, code review culture, and a strong bias toward shipping — with equal commitment to system reliability and customer experience.

  • Coach and grow senior/staff engineers into technical leaders; manage engineering managers as the organization scales.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure the platform evolves in lockstep with customer needs and market feedback.

Voice Platform & Agent QA

  • Own the end-to-end engineering for Ema’s AgentQA capabilities — real-time voice pipelines, telephony integrations, and voice-to-action workflows.

  • Build and scale the Agent QA platform: automated call scoring, compliance monitoring, sentiment analysis, and coaching feedback loops.

  • Design auto-learning systems that continuously improve voice agents from production interactions — closed-loop feedback, model retraining triggers, and quality regression detection.

  • Deliver rich voice analytics: call volume trends, handle time distributions, first-call resolution metrics, agent performance dashboards, and anomaly detection.

  • Build scalable voice pipeline across geographies – keeping in mind PII, security and compliance requirements.

Workforce Management & Operations Research

  • Build WFM capabilities including demand forecasting, shift scheduling, real-time adherence monitoring, and capacity planning — applying operations research techniques to optimize workforce utilization.

  • Design and implement optimization algorithms for headcount modeling, skill-based routing, and workload balancing across multi-site, multi-timezone contact center operations.

  • Partner with ML/AI teams to integrate predictive models for call volume forecasting, attrition risk, and staffing efficiency.

What We Look For

Required

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading engineering teams of 8+ engineers at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies.

  • Deep expertise in building real-time, data-intensive systems.

  • Strong foundation in data stores and storage systems: relational databases, time-series stores, columnar analytics engines, and caching layers — with the judgment to choose the right tool for the workload.

  • Experience building quality software using AI-driven tools and workflows.

  • Track record of taking products from 0→1 and iterating rapidly based on customer feedback.

  • Hands-on proficiency with SOLID principles, clean architecture, and design patterns — you write and review production code and lead by example on system design.

  • Experience building scalable multi-tenant SaaS platforms with data isolation, geo-distributed deployments, and compliance requirements (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA).

  • Track record of building ingestion systems for high volumes of load — event-driven architectures, stream processing (Kafka, Flink, or equivalent), and batch/real-time hybrid pipelines.

  • Strong product sense: ability to deeply understand customer problems in contact center, voice, and workforce domains and translate them into clean technical solutions.

  • Proven ability to hire, develop, and retain high-caliber engineers across multiple disciplines in competitive markets.

Good to have

  • Experience in voice/telephony systems: WebRTC, SIP, voice-over-IP infrastructure, or contact center platforms.

  • Background in operations research or optimization: scheduling algorithms, linear/integer programming, constraint satisfaction, or demand forecasting models.

  • Experience building analytics platforms: OLAP systems, real-time dashboards, metric computation engines, or BI infrastructure.

  • Prior work on auto-learning or continuous improvement systems: feedback loops from production data, automated retraining pipelines, or quality monitoring systems.

  • Experience with AI/ML-powered products in enterprise settings — agentic automation, LLM orchestration, or AI-driven UX.

  • Familiarity with WFM or contact center operations — staffing models, Erlang-based capacity planning, or real-time adherence systems.

Why Ema

  • Build at the intersection of Voice AI, operations research, and enterprise-scale systems — a rare combination of deeply technical challenges with direct customer impact.

  • Shape the engineering foundation of a category-defining AI platform — your architectural decisions will power how the world’s largest enterprises run their voice and workforce operations.

  • High-impact, high-visibility role with direct access to the Head of Engineering, co-founders, and enterprise customers.

  • A team of exceptional engineers from Google, Meta, Microsoft Research, and top CS programs worldwide.

  • Competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the opportunity to build something that matters.

title: Senior Conversion Design Analyst (f/m/d)
description:
Your mission

We're looking for a Senior Conversion Design Analyst who is genuinely both things: a designer who digs into data, and an analyst who designs. You decide with evidence. You will frame real user problems based on qualitative and quantitative data, design a part of our product, form a view about what should change, build the experiment that tests it, and analyze the results yourself.

You will sit inside the product delivery team that focuses on user growth, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it. And you will not be doing it alone: You join a group of Conversion Design Analysts across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards.

English is our working language. German matters here too: You will be designing flows that German-speaking users read.

Concretely, you will:

  • Design experiences grounded in real user needs and real neighbourhood life. Your job is to design flows and screens that are highly usable and intuitive and that earn their place by adding measurable value, not just because we can build them.
  • Frame the real problem before solving it. Dig into quantitative and qualitative data until you find the actual question underneath the ask. Then make it explainable and actionable. A well-framed problem is half the battle
  • Design, run the experiment, read it honestly and decide what comes next. Define a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome. Then use what you learned to frame the next question. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, and designing the next step.
  • Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.
  • Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do.
  • Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You will help decide what earns its place and what should be removed, and be willing to make the case for less.

Your profile

  • You practice product design and analytics. You might come from an analyst background and bring a love of design and design thinking, or vice versa.
  • You have run experiments end to end and know how to move from one to the next. Setting up the hypothesis, designing strong variants using our design system, choosing the right metrics to track, analyzing the results and then making a clear call on how to continue: ship it, kill it, or iterate.
  • You have technical know-how and experience in setting up and evaluating experiments in an A/B testing tool, constructing the needed dashboards for the problem space you are working on.
  • With sufficient data literacy, you get your own numbers through SQL query. You work with raw data to dig up insights and spot opportunities, without waiting for someone else to pull it for you.
  • You have statistical literacy. You don’t need to be able to run R, but you understand what Bayesian vs. frequentist is about and why you do a power analysis before launching an experiment.
  • You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about.
  • You present your work clearly, defend your decisions when challenged, and are comfortable in front of a crowd.
  • You are fluent with AI tools. This role allows you to have more control and impact through both design and analysis, but to do this well you'll need to leverage (and at times extend) our AI enablement stack
  • Excellent English skills for working in our international team.

To apply, include a cover letter explaining why this role and why now and if your background doesn't tick every box, tell us how you'd bridge the gap. Alongside it, share a portfolio that shows your work through its impact, at least one project walked through end to end: the hypothesis, what you designed, the result, and what you took from it. Show us how you used data to move your thinking forward, and where experimentation shaped what you built. If you can't share a portfolio due to an NDA or the nature of your work, a detailed cover letter walking through a project in the same way is fine.

Nice to have

  • Experience with a marketplace, community, classifieds, or other network product.
  • Strong German, or the confidence to design in it with support.
  • Experience building or maintaining parts of a design system.
  • Comfortable writing SQL without AI assistance.
  • You have basic dbt knowledge.

What we offer

  • Hybrid work model combining office and remote days
  • A meaningful job – we're creating a great product with real added value for the community
  • Work in a cheerful and experienced team that exchanges ideas and learns from each other
  • Insights into the entire work process of our social startup and the nebenan.de foundation
  • Responsibility and great opportunities to actively contribute
  • Your nebenan.de SpenditCard – you'll receive an additional income of 35 Euros per month, which you can use for things of your choice
  • 30 days of vacation per year – we also offer the possibility of workation models and a sabbatical
  • A workplace in Berlin-Kreuzberg and regular events like yoga or Lunch & Learn sessions.

If we’ve captured your interest, apply now and let us know why you’re the perfect fit for the job!

title: Responsable Qualité Multi-Sites - Piles à Combustible
description:
About EHG

Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

 

EH Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Global Quality Manager - Fuel Cell Manufacturing
description:
About EHG

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

title: Project Leider Bouw
description:
Monumental automatiseert de bouw met robotica en software. Onze missie is om de bouw software-defined en autonoom te maken – een toekomst waarin mooie gebouwen op maat in één dag verrijzen, met minimale inzet van handwerk.

We zijn een groeiend team van engineers, operators en technici, afkomstig van bedrijven als Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta en Google DeepMind. We staan nog aan het begin van het opbouwen van dit bedrijf, en dit is je kans om buitenproportioneel veel impact te maken op een probleem dat écht uitmaakt. Vanaf dag één werk je samen met een ervaren foundingteam, met een Series B van $32M achter ons onder leiding van Khosla Ventures en Plural.

Monumental zit in het centrum van Amsterdam, in een prachtig pand met een volledig uitgeruste werkplaats en een eigen testvloer voor robots. We bouwen de hele stack in-house – hardware én software. We zijn uitdrukkelijk geen hybride of remote-first bedrijf: robots en muren bouw je niet vanaf je keukentafel, dus we werken vijf dagen per week op locatie.

Lees meer over waarom wij vinden dat je je tijd aan de bouw zou moeten besteden, en over onze visie en ons bedrijf. Misschien vind je ons YouTube-kanaal interessant, de film van Based in Europe over hoe we het Europese woningtekort aanpakken, of deze video van Andreas Klinger over hoe ons kantoor eruitziet.

Over de functie

De afgelopen jaren is Monumental gegroeid van een werkend product en de eerste proefprojecten naar bouwen op grote schaal. Inmiddels hebben we een vloot van meer dan 150 robots, die metselwerk hebben uitgevoerd voor meer dan 90 woningen, een school, een buurthuis, een hotel en meer dan 150 meter kanaalwand.

Elke maand nemen we meer bouwprojecten aan, intern noemen we die ‘deployments’. We werken met meer robots en meer mensen en breiden vanuit Nederland uit naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk en de VS.

Als Hub Lead zet je onze eerste vestiging buiten het hoofdkantoor op, in het noorden van Nederland. Je begint met ons grootste bouwproject tot nu toe. Naarmate er meer projecten bijkomen, bouw je het team en de operatie verder uit.

We zoeken mensen die breed inzetbaar zijn en een bouwproject willen leiden alsof het hun eigen bedrijf is. Achter elk project staat een Deployment Manager die van begin tot eind verantwoordelijk is. In de praktijk vervul je vijf rollen tegelijk: uitvoerder, operationeel manager, accountmanager, analist en projectmanager. Je maakt het bouwplan, voert het met je team als onderaannemer uit, onderhoudt het contact met de aannemer en zorgt dat we goed metselwerk op tijd opleveren. Dat doe je in de bouw, waar plannen voortdurend veranderen. Uiteindelijk leid je meerdere projecten tegelijk, waaronder complexe projecten waarbij veel op het spel staat.

De ene dag sta je bij zonsopgang op en ga je naar de bouwplaats. Je zaagt stenen, bewaakt de planning, stemt af met de hoofdaannemer en ziet je bouwplan steen voor steen werkelijkheid worden. De volgende dag zit je op onze vestiging, analyseer je de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en werk je aan systemen waarmee je bij het volgende project een betere marge haalt. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de oplevering en geeft knelpunten die je op de bouwplaats tegenkomt door aan ons R&D-team.

Dit is intensief, praktisch werk op locatie, waar je veel voldoening uit kunt halen. Robots gaan kapot, het weer slaat om en de aannemer verandert het plan. Jij zorgt dat de bouw doorgaat.

Je krijgt veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. De rol past goed bij je als je eerder een bedrijf hebt opgericht, of als je een ondernemende functie zoekt waarin je veel invloed hebt op het resultaat.

Wat je gaat doen

  • De logistiek van een bouwproject plannen. Je bepaalt hoeveel en welke robots en mensen nodig zijn, stemt af met andere onderaannemers en maakt de dagelijkse planning. Tegelijk houd je het grotere geheel in het oog en begrijp je wat jouw keuzes betekenen voor de kosten en opbrengsten per project.

  • Op de bouwplaats het team aansturen, begeleiden en motiveren. Je onderhoudt het contact met hoofdaannemers en andere betrokkenen, vertegenwoordigt Monumental en legt uit wat we doen. Je schakelt net zo makkelijk met steigerbouwers als met de CEO’s van de grootste hoofdaannemers en onze engineers.

  • Operationele systemen opzetten waarmee elk project beter verloopt dan het vorige. Je ziet waar tijd en middelen verloren gaan, past processen aan en verbetert de marge.

  • Samenwerken met bestaande klanten en zorgen dat daar nieuwe bouwprojecten uit voortkomen. In de toekomst doe je dat ook voor aanverwante productlijnen buiten het metselwerk.

  • Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en voorstellen doen om de kosten en opbrengsten per project steeds verder te verbeteren.

  • Helpen bij het werven en interviewen van nieuwe robotoperators en deployment operators.

Wat we zoeken

  • Minimaal drie jaar ervaring startupervaring, als operator, manager, of founder.

  • Nederlands als moedertaal. De bouwsector is sterk lokaal georganiseerd, dus dit is een vereiste voor de functie.

  • Je communiceert helder en makkelijk met mensen met uiteenlopende achtergronden.

  • Je bent bereid om letterlijk je handen vuil te maken om het werk gedaan te krijgen.

  • Je komt snel in actie, zet door en krijgt dingen voor elkaar. In deze functie draait het vooral om uitvoeren.

  • Je kunt goed omgaan met hoge werkdruk. Op bouwplaatsen gaat regelmatig iets mis en staat er veel op het spel. Daar komt bij dat we nieuwe technologie inzetten waarvan we nog niet alle mogelijke storingen kennen.

  • Je denkt scherp en leert graag. Welke achtergrond je ook hebt, je zult in deze rol veel en snel moeten leren. Het werk kan elke drie tot zes maanden als een nieuwe baan voelen. Je leert veel over de bouw, robotica en werken in een snelgroeiend technologiebedrijf.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen van een klein team en weet hoe je mensen begeleidt en motiveert.

  • Je bent operationeel en analytisch sterk. Je kunt een helder operationeel plan uitwerken in een spreadsheet, een winst- en verliesrekening presenteren en verschillende scenario’s doorrekenen, inclusief de factoren die het resultaat bepalen. Je bent een sterke projectmanager.

Waarom Monumental?

Bij Monumental werken betekent vooroplopen in een beweging die de bouwsector wezenlijk wil veranderen. Jouw werk heeft hier niet alleen impact op het bedrijf, maar op de toekomst van hoe we bouwen. Als je gedreven wordt door innovatie, graag complexe uitdagingen aanpakt en klaar bent om echt verschil te maken, horen we graag van je.

Voor open sollicitaties (als je geen rol ziet die precies past) kun je ons mailen op:

Helaas bieden we op dit moment geen stageplekken aan.

Voldoe je niet aan alle eisen hierboven, maar ben je enthousiast over Monumental en denk je dat je ons toch kunt helpen moeilijke problemen op te lossen? Neem dan contact op. We verwelkomen generalisten die op resultaat gericht zijn en graag on the job leren.

As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the world. We cut through the noise and complexity of hotel and vacation rental booking, surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays — booked with confidence. With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology travelers can trust.

Who we're looking for

We are looking for a hands-on Quality Platform Lead to own Vio's quality strategy and automation platform across web, mobile, browser extensions, internal tooling and related surfaces.

This is a technical leadership role (Staff IC) reporting to the Director of Engineering. You define what good looks like for quality, decide where scarce testing effort goes, and give teams the confidence to ship. Your levers are release gates, quality telemetry, and a developer experience that makes the right tests easy to write and keep alive.

Product engineers own the tests for the features they build. Your remit is the platform, the strategy and the enablement that make that work hold up at scale. There is no QA department here and we have no plans to create one.

Where you'll start

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

The tooling can stay as it is. With a clear case you can migrate or rebuild. E2E coverage today is thin, so a different platform is genuinely on the table if it serves speed, maintainability and DX better. We have no predefined answer.

AI-assisted tooling is an open area too. We have no established practice for agent-generated tests or AI-assisted triage, so your judgment on what earns a place in the platform carries real weight.

What we lack today is clear ownership of strategy, release gates and shared quality telemetry, plus a low-friction path for engineers to spend their testing effort on the highest-risk scenarios.

How the role works

Your time splits between hands-on platform work, enablement, strategy and stakeholder telemetry. One insourced QA Engineer supports you. You own the technical direction, the standards and the quality outcomes.

Once the platform has low friction, product engineers write and maintain the tests for the domains they own. You enable that through patterns, docs, reusable modules, CI checks and risk-based guidance. Gatekeeping releases sits outside the role.

Expect no direct people-management responsibilities in the near future. Any further QE hire gets evaluated against the ~1:50 rule once the value is proven, and we have no committed headcount plan beyond that.

What you'll own

Quality strategy and platform

  • Own the quality strategy and the automation platform across products, covering direction, standards and day-to-day health

  • Decide whether to keep, evolve or replace the current tooling, with clear trade-offs on speed, maintainability and DX

  • Set coding standards and patterns for test code, and keep the suite focused on the tests that earn their place

Release gates and telemetry

  • Build automated release gates into CI/CD and define what protects the core journeys

  • Give Product, Engineering and leadership real-time quality telemetry on release readiness, risk and pipeline health

  • Put failure triage and flaky-test quarantine in place, so every failure is worth acting on

Risk-based coverage and testability

  • Work with Product and Engineering to protect high-impact journeys and APIs

  • Retire flaky and low-value tests, and concentrate effort where the risk is highest

  • Act as the technical stakeholder for testability (hooks, mocks, contract tests, test data) and get those improvements onto team roadmaps

Developer enablement

  • Make it easy for product engineers to write, run and maintain tests locally and in CI

  • Embed quality into how teams plan and ship, and mentor the insourced QA Engineer

  • Drive a measurable increase in developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX

What success looks like in 12 months

  1. Platform ownership. You have taken over the automation platform across products and own it outright, with direction, standards and health all unambiguous, whether you kept the tooling or replaced it.

  2. Gates and focus. Release gates on the core journeys are fast and deterministic, and testing effort sits on the highest-risk scenarios.

  3. Dev ownership and satisfaction. Writing and maintaining tests is a routine part of Definition of Done, and developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX has measurably improved.

  4. Telemetry. Eng and Product work from live release-readiness and risk dashboards, failures triage cleanly, and flaky tests go into quarantine.

  5. Less manual drag. Regular releases go out without manual testing, with exploratory testing reserved for major new work.

Who you are

  • You have a track record of building or overhauling automation platforms (SWE / QE / SDET)

  • You write production-grade code across app, test and infra repos. Language matters less to us than depth, though our stack today leans on TypeScript/JS, Elixir, Go, Python and Dart.

  • You use AI agents effectively in your own engineering workflow and can judge where they belong inside a quality platform, from test generation to failure triage

  • You have cross-platform web and mobile automation judgment, and can weigh unified toolchains against separate ones objectively

  • You have deep CI/CD and test infrastructure experience: GitHub Actions, device clouds, parallelisation, test data

  • You can translate quality risk into telemetry and decisions that Eng, Product and leadership act on

  • You are a hands-on builder who wants to code the platform yourself

  • You design platforms developers adopt, and you prioritise risk-based coverage

Trade-offs we accept: depth on one platform when the other is learnable, and no travel or booking domain background.

Why join us now?

  • Full ownership of the quality strategy and the automation platform, with a mandate for enablement

  • We are one of the most innovative and fastest-growing accommodation booking platforms in the world today, having grown our bookings 30x between 2017 and 2025, and catering to the needs of over 100 million unique visitors worldwide each year. We do that by harnessing the power of advanced algorithms and an innovative suite of power features and managed to overcome the corona crisis remarkably fast;

  • The mobile applications (iOS and Android) we launched in 2023 are already a big success, reaching 5 million installs with great customer reviews, as we are beginning to build Vio as the brand for value-seeking travellers worldwide;

  • We are a passionate and diverse team of tech enthusiasts and creatives with a commitment and focus on the traveler above all else - and it shows in our industry-leading TrustPilot score;

  • We place huge importance on rewarding our employees for the value they generate by giving Stock Appreciation Rights to all employees.

Do you want to know if Vio is the right place for you? Find out by reading about the attitude that thrives at Vio.

What we offer:

  • Plenty of chances to learn and grow within an open, diverse culture which promotes knowledge sharing, trust and transparency;

  • A great compensation package, perks and benefits (including significant stock appreciation rights);

  • Flexible time off (take as many holidays as you need) and a chance to work remotely;

  • You will be part of a highly international team that enjoys working, eating and playing together in one of the best office locations in Amsterdam;

  • We value good food and offer catered lunches from various cuisines, great coffee, and the occasional barbecue in our garden;

  • We enjoy getting together to celebrate our wins with company events in Amsterdam and abroad;

  • A budget for your dream home office;

  • Access to free mental health support via OpenUp.

Working cross-functionally with Data Engineering, Product, Clinical Operations, and EMR partners, your solutions will transform how clinicians access dataâmoving from external tools and workarounds to seamless, in-workflow decision support via CDS Hooks and real-time APIs.

This role sits at the intersection of healthcare interoperability standards, modern API design, and operational excellence.   • Establish API contracts, versioning strategies, and deprecation policies that balance innovation with stability for external consumers

  • Implement and maintain API security patterns including OAuth 2.0, scope-based authorization, rate limiting, and audit logging for compliant clinical data access

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience designing, building, and operating API platforms, service-oriented systems, or backend infrastructure at scale

In this role, you'll own the platform that takes our data, models and estimation methods from R&D to auditable client deliverables, and you'll be a trusted reviewer and guide across software and data engineering. You'll work closely with fellow software and data engineers, data scientists and solutions engineers, turning research code into robust, reproducible infrastructure. You will join a cross-functional, mission-driven team dedicated to bringing transparency and integrity to climate action.

Impact you’ll own:

  • Shorten the path from experiment to production: own how models and estimation features move from research into reproducible, auditable client deliverables, with data, models and environments versioned end to end.

  • Own our developer platform and engineering standards: environments, containers, project templates, CI/CD and pipeline orchestration across a multi-repo Python stack.

  • Own our GCP infrastructure: architecture, infrastructure-as-code, monitoring, cost and access management, and its evolution as the company grows.

  • Shape our geospatial workflows: how we store and process vector and high-resolution raster data at scale, and how the databases behind our models and deliverables evolve as we scale.

  • Be the key reviewer for core and pipeline infra: write design docs for your own areas and review those of others, keeping our architecture coherent as the team grows.

  • Raise the bar across engineering: mentor other engineers, and support our software & data engineering team with feedback and guidance on design and architecture.

  • Over time, coordinate our infrastructure development goals: set priorities and align work across software and data engineering.

What you bring:

  • 6+ years of experience in engineering roles, including significant time designing and running data-intensive backend systems and pipelines in production

  • A track record of owning systems end to end: you've made architectural decisions and lived with their consequences, written and reviewed design docs, and mentored other engineers

  • Expert Python and strong SQL, with solid experience designing schemas and data models for production systems

  • Hands-on experience with workflow and pipeline tooling (e.g. Airflow, Dagster), experiment tracking and data versioning

  • Hands-on experience running production cloud infrastructure, ideally GCP; infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform/OpenTofu), IAM, as well as containers and reproducible environments (e.g. Docker, devcontainers)

  • A degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

What makes you stand out:

  • Production experience with raster data and geospatial pipelines

  • Experience building model serving, model registries or other MLOps tooling (e.g. DVC, MLFlow)

  • Experience building BI or dashboarding tooling (e.g. Streamlit) for non-technical users

  • Experience with data warehouse design (e.g. BigQuery, PostgreSQL, dbt) and data engineering workflows

  • Previous exposure to earth observation, environmental monitoring or soil science data

title: Lead Data Engineer
description:
We help companies get compensation right.

What we get paid at work has a massive impact on our lives, and it’s one of the biggest factors in hiring and retaining talent - and yet so many companies struggle to get it right. They simply have no choice but to rely on poor data and unsophisticated tools for their pay decisions. That’s why we created Ravio.

We help many of the world’s most innovative and ambitious companies build stronger teams and reach their goals through better compensation. Our real-time data platform brings compensation into the modern age, tracking the market across all compensation types from salary to equity and benefits. We’re passionate about ensuring everyone is paid what they deserve, no matter their background or circumstances. We believe that when compensation is done right, everyone wins.

Ravio is growing fast, which means you can too. We’ve established ourselves as the European leader in our space serving more than 1,200 clients, and now have our sights set on becoming the global go to place for compensation data and tools for managing compensation.

Joining a startup and scaling it into a global product is one of the most challenging and rewarding experiences a career can offer. If that sounds exciting to you, you’re in the right place.

The role

We’re looking for a Lead Data Engineer to lead a small team of data engineers within our Engineering team. You’ll remain hands-on in designing, building, and operating the data systems behind our compensation benchmarks, customer-facing tools, and AI agents. You’ll take a platform engineering approach to data, building reliable, reusable capabilities that help Engineering, Data Science, and Insights deliver. You’ll combine technical leadership with line management and coaching, working with engineering and product colleagues to turn priorities into delivered outcomes.

You’ll report to our VP Engineering.

Hands-on engineering and delivery

  • Be a senior technical contributor, building and operating the pipelines, integrations, and data services behind Ravio’s product. Design clear interfaces between ingestion, transformation, and downstream applications so teams can build on trusted data without bespoke support for every change.

  • Shape and deliver the data roadmap with Product, Data Science, and Insights. Prioritise improvements that deliver customer value, reduce recurring manual work, or address reliability needs, while keeping complexity and cloud costs under control.

  • Build data quality, governance, and security into everyday delivery through automated checks, clear data ownership, and appropriate access controls.

  • Work with engineering colleagues to integrate data systems into shared development, deployment, and monitoring practices. Use version-controlled transformations, automated tests, and repeatable deployments, reducing bespoke tooling where it adds unnecessary overhead.

  • Own the reliability and day-to-day support of the team’s production data systems, improving monitoring and recovery. Build reusable ingestion patterns and self-service workflows around recurring needs, measuring their value through faster delivery, fewer failures, and less manual support.

  • Use AI-assisted tools for development, testing, documentation, and investigation. Help the team use them effectively, with appropriate review of outputs and protection of customer data.

Team management and leadership

  • Lead the team’s delivery planning and ways of working, keeping priorities, scope, and dependencies visible. Take part in shared product prioritisation, bringing requests from Data Science, Insights, and Operations into an agreed delivery plan.

  • Partner with software engineers, product managers, and data colleagues to make timely decisions and share responsibility for delivered outcomes.

  • Line manage and coach a small team of data engineers, providing regular feedback and supporting their technical and career development.

  • Build a supportive, accountable team with shared ownership of its systems. Use pairing, code reviews, documentation, and operational handovers to spread knowledge.

What we’re looking for

  • Six-plus years’ experience in data engineering, with at least two years in a team leadership role.

  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building and operating production data systems.

  • Experience with data modelling, transformation frameworks such as dbt, and workflow orchestration.

  • Experience applying platform engineering principles to data systems, such as reusable ingestion patterns, clear data interfaces, or self-service tooling that other teams use successfully.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, automated testing, and continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD).

  • Practical understanding of reliable data processing, including schema changes, retries, safe reprocessing, and backfills.

  • Experience using monitoring and data quality checks to investigate failures and improve reliability.

  • Practical use of AI-assisted engineering tools, with sound judgement about verification, security, and where automation adds value.

  • Proven ability to mentor engineers, set team goals, and deliver value for users and the business.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment with a bias for action.

  • Excellent listening and communication skills.

How you work

  • You speak the language of engineers and data scientists, and are comfortable working with Product, Customer Success, Operations, and founders.

  • You bring empathy and strong social and emotional intelligence, with an ability to put yourself in others’ shoes.

  • You take satisfaction in solving challenging problems and helping a talented team deliver effectively.

Our tech stack

Data Engineering

  • Python and SQL

  • dbt for data transformations

  • dlt for data extraction and loading

  • Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Cloud Functions, Workflows, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, and Datastream

  • PostgreSQL

Data Science

  • Python (polars, pandas, scikit)

  • Jupyter notebooks

  • SQL and dbt

Infrastructure and delivery

  • GitHub Actions

  • Terraform

  • Artifact Registry

Data engineering at Ravio

Data is central to Ravio’s product. As we expand our compensation tools and build AI-powered experiences, we need reliable ways to bring customer data in and make it available across the platform.

You’ll help a small team deliver that work alongside software engineers, data scientists, and product colleagues. Success means useful capabilities reaching customers, dependable data for colleagues, and less time spent on avoidable support and manual processes.

Why join Ravio?

  • Opportunity to be a critical team member in a high-growth startup.

  • A blend of hands-on engineering and leadership, giving you both direct impact and career growth.

  • Remote-friendly, flexible work culture with a high degree of ownership.

  • Work on meaningful problems that help people get paid fairly and competitively in their careers.

Compensation and benefits

  • £100,000 - £120,000 salary

  • Company ownership (everyone gets a meaningful equity stake in Ravio)

  • 37 days paid time off (25 days holiday + 4 wellness days + 8 public holidays)

  • Up to 6% pension matching scheme

  • £60 a month wellness allowance (Invest in your physical wellbeing, on us)

  • Private healthcare cover (on a medical history disregarded basis) with AXA

  • Personal worldwide travel insurance - just in case

  • Income protection insurance (for full peace of mind in case you cannot work because of sickness or disability)

  • 16 weeks fully paid birthing parent leave, followed by 4 weeks at 50% pay. For non-birthing parents, we offer 8 weeks fully paid leave.

description:
Before jumping into all the information about the role and what you can bring to the table, let us introduce ourselves real quick.

About us

Insider One is the #1 platform that brings everything marketing and customer engagement teams need in one place so they can reach their peak potential and become unstoppable. 

Our story began with six desks and a vision to create a single platform to make industry-first technologies and emerging channels accessible to marketers worldwide. title: Engineering Manager
description:
About Stora

Stora is building the operating platform for modern self-storage businesses.

Our software helps operators manage bookings, payments, customers, facilities and day-to-day operations from one place, while automating much of the work that traditionally makes running a self-storage business unnecessarily complicated.

In just over five years, Stora has grown from an early-stage product into a platform used by more than 500 operators.

We’re a product-led, remote-first company with an experienced engineering team and ambitious plans for what comes next.

Now, as the engineering organisation grows, we’re hiring an Engineering Manager to make sure the way we lead, develop and support engineers grows with it.

The Role

This is a genuine people leadership role.

You’ll manage approximately 12 engineers working across three product teams, with the team expected to continue growing.

Each product team has a Tech Lead responsible for technical direction, alongside Product and Design. Your focus is different: the engineers themselves.

This isn’t a role for somebody looking to move away from engineering completely, though. You’ll need enough technical depth to understand the work, follow engineering discussions and ask good questions without needing to be the person making every technical decision.

You’ll work closely with our Head of Engineering and have support from People, but you’ll have meaningful autonomy to improve how engineering management works at Stora.

What Else You’ll Own

Engineering Management

  • Manage engineers across multiple product teams through regular, useful 1:1s, coaching and clear feedback.

  • Make expectations clear and help engineers understand what good performance looks like.

  • Identify performance issues early and handle difficult conversations properly when needed.

  • Support engineers in progressing from junior through senior and beyond.

  • Build strong relationships with engineers without creating unnecessary management overhead.

Performance & Progression

  • Own the engineering performance and progression approach.

  • Review and improve our existing career levels, expectations and review processes.

  • Make promotion and progression decisions that are consistent, evidence-based and understood by the team.

  • Create a culture where feedback happens throughout the year rather than being saved for formal reviews.

Hiring & Team Development

  • Own engineering hiring alongside the relevant Tech Leads and wider team.

  • Help define what we need before a search begins, assess candidates properly and maintain a high hiring bar.

  • Ensure new engineers have a structured and useful onboarding experience.

  • Think proactively about team composition, capability gaps and future hiring needs.

Team Health

  • Pay attention to engagement, retention, collaboration and emerging people issues across the engineering organisation.

  • Work with Tech Leads when team problems sit somewhere between technical delivery, behaviour and team dynamics.

  • Help maintain a strong remote engineering culture as Stora grows.

Technical Context

  • Stay close enough to the engineering work to understand what the team is solving and the environment they’re working within.

  • Be comfortable reading code, following pull requests and participating intelligently in technical conversations.

  • Partner with Tech Leads without competing with them for technical ownership.

What Success Looks Like

After your first year, we’d expect:

  • Engineers to have a clear understanding of what is expected of them and how they can progress.

  • Managers and engineers to be having better, more useful conversations about performance and development.

  • Performance issues to be addressed early rather than becoming surprises.

  • A progression framework that works for the engineering organisation Stora has become, not the company we were several years ago.

  • Stronger and more consistent hiring and onboarding.

  • The Head of Engineering spending less time acting as the default people manager for the entire engineering organisation.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager, rather than somebody taking their first step into management.

You’ll ideally have:

  • Previous experience directly managing software engineers across more than one team or product area.

  • A strong track record of developing engineers at different stages of their careers.

  • Hands-on experience managing performance, including difficult or underperformance situations.

  • Experience making promotion and progression decisions.

  • Experience running or improving engineering career frameworks, review cycles or progression processes.

  • Previous experience hiring software engineers and building effective interview processes.

  • An engineering background that allows you to understand code and contribute meaningfully to technical conversations.

  • The judgement to know when to get involved and when to leave technical decisions with the Tech Leads.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in a remote environment.

  • A practical understanding of how AI tools are changing software engineering and experience using them in your own work.

Experience with Ruby or Rails would be useful, but it isn’t essential.

We’re much more interested in whether you can lead engineers well.

What This Role Isn’t

It’s worth being clear that this isn’t:

  • a Tech Lead role with some people management added on;

  • a delivery or project management position;

  • a Product Manager role;

  • a hands-on engineering role where you’ll spend most of your week writing production code;

  • a first Engineering Manager opportunity.

Technical leadership already exists within the product teams.

We’re hiring you because engineering management itself deserves dedicated ownership.

Our Technology

You won’t be expected to spend most of your time writing production code, but you should be comfortable working around our stack.

Backend: Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, TimescaleDB

Frontend: Turbo, React, ViewComponents, Sass

Testing: Minitest, Playwright

Deployment: GitHub Actions, Heroku

Salary & Benefits

  • Salary: Highly competitive and depending on experience

  • Location: Fully remote within the UK or Ireland

  • Belfast office: Available for anyone who wants to use it

  • Private health insurance for you and your family

  • Company pension

  • 35 days’ annual leave inclusive of applicable public/statutory holidays, depending on location

  • Learning and development support

  • Share options

title: Senior Product Manager, Panel (Remote, EU/UK)
description:
About Maze

Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values.

Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal.

Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.

About the Role

Maze customers need to reach the right participants and trust the quality of the people taking part in their studies. Recruitment is a critical part of research.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the recruitment and panel experience at Maze. You’ll help shape how customers recruit and manage participants across unmoderated, moderated, AI-moderated and future research experiences.

This is a highly cross-functional product area that sits at the intersection of product, operations and our panel partner ecosystem. You’ll work in a trio with Engineering and Design while partnering closely with our Panel Operations team, GTM, Customer Success, Research Partners and other product teams.

You’ll own the customer and participant experiences as well as the systems behind them, helping Maze deliver a recruitment experience that is high-quality, reliable and able to scale with increasingly complex customer needs.

You’ll work on:

  • Own and evolve the roadmap for recruitment and participant management across Maze.

  • Improve participant quality by building stronger feedback loops, quality signals, filtering and experiences that reduce confusion for participants.

  • Make it easier for customers to recruit the audiences they need across different study types, including more complex enterprise use cases.

  • Use data and customer insights to understand panel performance and identify gaps in participant supply, quality and fulfillment.

  • Partner with Panel Operations to continuously improve the tools, workflows and handoffs used to fulfill recruitment requests.

  • Help evaluate and onboard new panel partners and identify where deeper integrations can improve quality, coverage or efficiency.

  • Develop smarter ways to route studies to the right participant supply based on customer and study needs.

  • Stay close to the operational side of recruitment so product decisions are grounded in how participant fulfillment actually happens.

  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success and Research Partners to understand customer needs, recruitment feasibility and opportunities to improve the recruitment experience.

  • Define and measure success across participant quality, fulfillment and the overall recruitment experience.

You should apply if:

  • You have experience as a Product Manager or Senior Product Manager owning meaningful product areas from discovery through execution.

  • You’re highly autonomous and comfortable taking a problem, creating structure around it and driving it forward without waiting for perfect direction.

  • You’re a clear, structured communicator who can bring others along in how you think about a problem, recommendation or decision.

  • You’re comfortable working on products that span software, operations and external partners rather than living entirely within a single product surface.

  • You’re comfortable getting close to operational workflows and using what you learn to make better product decisions.

  • You have strong product judgment and can make thoughtful tradeoffs when there isn’t a perfect answer.

  • You’re experienced partnering closely with Engineering and Design to take products from discovery through delivery and iteration.

  • You think in systems and look for scalable product solutions rather than one-off workarounds.

  • You’re comfortable balancing customer experience, business needs, operational realities and technical constraints.

  • You thrive in an environment where you can move quickly, make decisions with imperfect information and continuously learn from customers and internal teams.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Strong data fluency and experience using data to understand problems, prioritize opportunities and measure product outcomes.

  • Experience building products with a meaningful operational component.

  • Marketplace or supply-and-demand product experience.

  • Experience in operations, business development or other roles that required you to work across product and business problems.

  • Experience managing stakeholders across multiple teams or functions.

  • Experience working with external partners, vendors or integrations that are critical to the customer experience.

  • Experience with user research or research participant recruitment.

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture. 

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

  • Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

  • Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

  • Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Benefits

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits here.

We understand you might be excited about the job you’re applying for, we are excited you are interested! Nebuly is a fast-growing, VC-backed startup building the platform that proves the ROI of enterprise AI.

Who we are

Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.

We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.

Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role

Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth.

It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there.

You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day.

  • Review and embed Yubo's Crisis Comms Playbook.

  • Build Yubo's 2027 PR calendar and strategy, balancing campaigns, cultural moments, and day-to-day press activity.

  • Team up with Product and Data to build proof points and stories that show what Yubo means to people.

  • Work with Trust & Safety and Legal so Yubo talks about sensitive topics responsibly.

  • Help rally the right people internally when a crisis hits.

Who you are

You're a proactive PR lead with sharp cultural instincts and a track record of creating stories that genuinely earn attention, not just promote launches.

You'll bring:

  • Solid PR experience, with real results to show from leading a function or campaign.

  • A good read on Gen-Z culture and how 18 to 24 year-olds socialise and engage online.

  • Experience turning insight and data into media stories, including digging into data yourself to find the angle.

  • A track record of using different levers to earn attention: influencers, experts, events, activations, research, stunts.

  • Experience managing and getting the best out of an external PR agency.

  • Good judgement under pressure, with experience in issues or crisis communications.

  • Strong writing and speaking skills, comfortable with both consumer storytelling and sensitive corporate messaging.

  • The ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.

  • A self-starter mindset, with examples of building something from the ground up.

Nice to have, but don't let that stop you:

  • Experience in high-growth tech, consumer apps, youth culture, media, entertainment or lifestyle.

  • Experience in the US market, including relationships with US media and journalists.

Within a month, you will

  • Get familiar with Yubo's product, mission and community, and where our communications and reputation stand today.

  • Meet key people across Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal.

  • Start onboarding our PR agency and reviewing the Crisis Comms Playbook.

Within 3 months, you will

  • Have set up solid working habits with the PR agency and cross-functional teams.

  • Be well into building the 2027 PR strategy, calendar and measurement framework.

  • Have embedded the Crisis Comms Playbook and be actively building relationships with consumer, culture, lifestyle, tech and business media.

Within 6 months, you will

  • Have delivered Yubo's finished 2027 PR strategy and calendar.

  • Have landed our first standout data- and culture-led stories in top-tier media, backed by a working way to measure PR performance.

  • Have wrapped up the agency onboarding and defined the role of creators, experts, events and activations in Yubo's communications, leaving a solid foundation for what's next.

The recruitment process

  • A first introductory call with Nicolas, Talent Acquisition

  • A case study with Alex, our Brand Director.

Our approach to privacy & safety

As part of your role, you may handle tools and features involving personal data. We expect all employees to demonstrate strong awareness of privacy and safety issues, and to actively support our Privacy & Safety by Design efforts.

Join Yubo and help shape the future of Social Discovery while enjoying a culture that values flexibility, well-being, and impact.

 

Here’s how we live our mission every day:

You own the impact: Step up, adapt, and make it matter

Unconventionally Smart: Hack with intent, borrow smart, build better

Be Bold & Resilient: Raise your head, break barriers, keep moving forward

One team, one mission: No egos, no passengers, just shared wins

 

Trust & Flexibility: Our hybrid model calls for only two office days a month; the rest is up to the rhythm that works best for you.

 

Enjoy Top-notch Benefits

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager with real technical depth and an AI-first way of working. You'll own a product area end to end: finding problems worth solving, shaping the solution, taking it from 0 to 1 and growing it from there.
You understand architecture, you've written code, you know how databases work, and you speak engineering fluently. Your main job is product. The technical depth is what lets you move faster and make better calls.
AI isn't a feature we're adding. It's how we work and how we build. Expect roughly 70% product and 30% engineering, with full accountability for results.


Your Mission

  • Product direction: set the vision, strategy and roadmap for your area. Decide what to build, why, and how success is measured.
  • 0-to-1 delivery: take new products and features from problem discovery to launch and iteration.
  • Discovery and validation: work directly with users and data to understand real problems, not assumed ones. Run interviews, usability tests and experiments before committing to build.
  • Metrics and outcomes: define, instrument and track the KPIs for your area. Use product analytics to find friction, prioritise the highest-impact work, and shut down what doesn't work.
  • Engineering partnership: understand architectural trade-offs, review technical approaches and unblock decisions. Write specs engineers actually want to read: clear, technical and opinionated.
  • AI and automation: find where LLMs and agents create real product value, build the case, and ship it.
  • Fast prototyping: validate ideas with AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, agents), scripts, no-code, or whatever gets you to the answer quickest.
  • Hands-on work: write queries, dig into data pipelines, spin up prototypes, and open a PR when it makes sense.
  • Prioritisation: balance user impact, business value, effort and regulatory constraints, and work closely with Engineering, Design, Analytics and business owners to ship continuously.


Your Profile

  • 5+ years in product management or product engineering with strong technical involvement, and a track record of taking products from 0 to live use with real users.
  • AI-native: you use LLMs, vibe coding and agents daily, and you've applied LLMs or agentic AI to real products.
  • Strong in Python or a similar language, enough to build things yourself. Comfortable with SQL, git, databases and evaluating system architecture.
  • Fluent in product analytics and research: you define metrics, read data yourself, and validate through interviews, usability testing and experiments.
  • Strong grasp of UX. You can take a complex flow and make it simple.
  • Experience shipping with Design and Engineering in an agile environment.
  • Clear communicator in English and self-directed. You can explain technical decisions to non-technical people, write specs engineers respect, and don't wait to be told what matters.

Nice to Have
  • Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical field.
  • Experience in fintech or another regulated industry.
  • Early-stage startup background.
  • Hands-on LLM orchestration or prompt engineering.
  • Background in software engineering, QA or product analytics.


Why Join Vivid?

  • We have a hybrid model in our Limassol and Berlin offices, or fully remote outside office locations. 
  • We support relocation to Cyprus (visa, package) when needed.
  • AI-first culture – we use it every day, not just talk about it.
  • Learning & development budget to support your professional growth. 
  • Fully paid vacation and sick leave. 
  • Sports compensation. 
  • Real growth prospects, significant responsibility, and the ability to make an immediate impact from day one.


Compensation range

Final compensation is determined individually, based on your experience, skills and the scope of the role, assessed against objective, gender-neutral criteria.


About Vivid

At Vivid, we're on a mission to change how businesses and individuals manage their money across Europe. For businesses, we build tools that actually make a difference: multi-IBAN accounts, high-yield savings, business cashback, team cards, and accounting integrations that save real time — all in one place. And for individuals, we offer a simple way to manage and grow your wealth: access to global stocks, ETFs and 150+ cryptocurrencies, cashback, and personalised financial insights.

Our mission? Your success. Everyone deserves the chance to see their finances flourish, and we're dedicated to empowering our customers to make this a reality.

Founded in 2019 in Berlin by Alexander Emeshev and Artem Iamanov, Vivid has quickly grown into one of Germany's top financial platforms for SMEs and private accounts. Since then, we've expanded rapidly across Europe, earning the trust of over 500,000 customers — and with over €200 million raised and a valuation of €775 million, we're just getting started.

We're building Vivid as an AI-native organization — across every function, from product to compliance to operations. Automation handles a growing share of day-to-day execution. For us, this means our teams can focus on architecture, strategy, and high-impact decision-making. This changes how we work: less manual execution, more ownership in building systems that scale. We want to help define what AI-native looks like in a regulated financial environment — and we're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

Finom is a European tech startup headquartered in Amsterdam, and we’re on a journey towards revolutionizing the financial landscape for entrepreneurs worldwide.
